transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Devon (Redwood SE), Alex (Horizon Eng Lead), Priya (Horizon CTO), Samir (Horizon Platform)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be short):
- Demo focused on migration playbook from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API.
- Walkthrough of Console, routing, Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization), and parity mapping matrix.
- Agreed next steps: send mapping/cost sheet, run benchmarks, schedule private deployment scoping.

Topics: API parity mapping, Console routing/fallbacks, Redwood Optimize recommendations, SOC2/KMS, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, latency/cost SLOs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, with Carlos and Devon from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Alex: Good, thanks. We got a short agenda — we're trying to figure out the migration path from OpenAI and Anthropic endpoints into something that matches our latency and cost targets.
[00:14] Priya: Yeah and security is obviously huge for us, want to understand private deployment and KMS integration.
[00:20] Carlos: Perfect. We'll go through a high-level playbook, show the Console, then run through Optimize's recommendations and finally map the parity matrix between the models you run today and the closest Redwood-verified variants.
[00:32] Samir: Quick note — we also have some Together models in the stack for research, so curious how Redwood handles multi-vendor parity and fallbacks.
[00:38] Maya: Good call out. We'll show routing policies that can do region-based or cost-based routing and automatic fallbacks to compatible model families.
[00:45] Alex: Alright, let's jump in.

[02:10] Carlos: (screen share) Ok, first the Console. Top left you see an endpoints list; each endpoint ties to a model and a route policy. You can pin a model version and then set rollout policy: canary, A/B, automatic fallback.
[02:28] Devon: We also capture token-level latency and cost breakdowns per request so you can see where the expense is. That helps with Optimize suggestions later.
[02:40] Priya: How granular is the RBAC? We need segregation between dev/prod and telemetry access for auditors.
[02:46] Carlos: RBAC is role-based SSO/SAML integrated. You can set read-only audit viewers, full admin, and restricted deploy roles. Audit logs are immutable and exportable.
[02:58] Alex: Is that part of Private or Hosted?
[03:02] Maya: Both. Hosted offers SSO + audit logs; Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you a private control plane plus KMS/HSM integrations for key management, and audit visibility is retained.

[05:15] Carlos: Now the Optimize tab — it runs a short analysis of traffic patterns and suggests batching levels, KV prefix caching rules, and suggested quantization profiles by workload. Example: for short-chat user flows we recommended aggressive KV caching and smaller batch windows to keep p99 latency under 120ms.
[05:36] Alex: How does KV-cache interact with rolling updates? If we roll a model, do cache keys invalidate?
[05:43] Devon: Good question. Cache entries are keyed by model-version plus prompt prefix; when you switch active model version, you can choose to preserve compatible cache (same tokenizer/embedding) or invalidate. We can automate fallback logic too.

[08:00] Priya: On the parity mapping — we run OpenAI for completions, Anthropic for safety heavy flows, and Together for research. We need a mapping table that shows approximate latency, token cost, and failure modes when mapped to Redwood variants.
[08:18] Maya: We'll provide a matrix. Quick example off the top: OpenAI gpt-4-style -> Redwood x-large (fp16/qat) with recommended quantization profile Q4_0 or Q4_1 depending on quality target; Anthropic Claude-like -> Redwood safety-tuned variant; Together-v -> Redwood experimental family, might be slightly lower throughput depending on architecture.
[08:45] Samir: The customers sometimes see hallucination differences between models; will Redwood provide eval tooling to compare outputs?
[08:52] Carlos: Yes. Evals integration is in Console — you can push a labeled prompt set and run regression checks. Optimize will flag quality regressions tied to prompt sets and suggest model/quantization changes.

[11:10] Alex: Cost is big. Give us a concrete per-1k token delta we'd expect if we move from hosted OpenAI to Redwood hosted.
[11:18] Maya: We'll send a tailored cost worksheet, but ballpark: with batching and KV-cache we often see 30-60% unit cost reduction for retrieval/assistant flows. Exact depends on sequence length distribution.
[11:29] Priya: What's the typical latency SLO you can hit for short chat (<= 128 tokens)? Our p95 target is 150ms.
[11:36] Carlos: On Dedicated GPU pools we routinely hit p95 < 120ms for 2k context in many models when configured with warm KV cache and optimal kernels; on Hosted multi-tenant it depends on tier, but the dedicated option is the safer bet for tight SLOs.

[13:50] Samir: Can you walk through an example of a fallback policy? Say OpenAI hits quota, we want to fall back to Together, and then to Redwood smaller variant.
[13:59] Devon: In the Console you attach a routing policy to an endpoint. You can set a priority list: primary model -> secondary model -> cost-fallback. Policies can be triggered by latency thresholds, error rates, or capacity alerts. We also support traffic splitting so you can A/B a fallback first.
[14:24] Alex: Ok that helps. What about data residency — some EU customers require logs to remain in region.
[14:32] Carlos: We have region-aware routing and retention policies per endpoint. For Private deployments, the data never leaves the VPC unless you opt in. For Hosted, you can pick region and retention window.

[17:05] Priya: Security checklist: SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs. Can you share the pack?
[17:12] Maya: Yes, we'll drop the compliance bundle link after the call. We'll also share integration notes for AWS KMS and customer-managed keys.

[19:48] Carlos: Now a quick demo of the API parity mapping doc — (shares spreadsheet) first column is your current vendor & model, second column is Redwood candidate, third is expected latency delta, fourth is token cost estimate, fifth is known functional diffs, sixth is migration notes.
[20:10] Alex: That kind of table is exactly what we need. On the 'functional diffs' row, can you capture safety/scoring differences for Anthropic -> Redwood?
[20:19] Carlos: We'll include a qualitative note and link to evals runs. For stronger fidelity, we can run a filtered subset of your safety prompts and report side-by-side outputs.

[22:55] Devon: Quick note on quantization: some model families map cleanly to int4/qat (we call out Q4_0/Q4_1), others we recommend int8 hybrid. Optimize will recommend the profile and show expected perf/cost tradeoff.
[23:12] Priya: Will quantization change outputs? We can't have regression in critical flows.
[23:18] Carlos: There are small differences sometimes; that's why we tie quantization suggestions to prompt-set evals and regression alerts. You can keep warm canaries on FP16 while testing Q4 canaries.

[26:40] Alex: For the Together models — latency was... inconsistent in our tests. Any particular kernel or hardware you'd recommend?
[26:48] Carlos: Together models with long context benefit from A100-like memory bandwidth; some newer Ampere/Grace-like stacks vary. Our runtime will choose kernels by heuristic based on architecture, seq length distribution; we'll include a recommended hardware SKU for your expected load in the mapping doc.

[29:00] Priya: About the bench runs — what do you need from us?
[29:05] Maya: If you can share a 200-500 prompt seed set and a small representative traffic trace (anonymized), Carlos can run the 3-model bench on Redwood hosted and Dedicated simulations and return a CSV with p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, and cost estimates.
[29:19] Samir: We can do that. We'll need to anonymize internal PII but the shapes should be fine.

[31:40] Carlos: Demoing route config: here's a route that sends 80% traffic to primary, 20% to canary; if error rate > 5% in 2 minutes, auto-fallback to secondary; you can set capacity-based routing such that when Dedicated pool is saturated it spills over to hosted at lower priority.
[31:59] Alex: Is there automated alerting into PagerDuty?
[32:04] Devon: Yup — we support webhooks, built-in integrations to Datadog, Prometheus, and PagerDuty.

[34:30] Priya: Cost spreadsheets often hide the caching benefits; can you show a model of how Optimize translates KV-cache hit rate to token delta?
[34:38] Carlos: (shares chart) If you have an 80% KV hit rate on prefix caching for retrieval flows, token consumption can drop by ~70% because you avoid regen for prefix content; Optimize will simulate hit/miss scenarios using your trace to project cost.

[37:50] Alex: Any gotchas with embeddings and vector search? We currently store vectors with OpenAI embeddings and use an external vector DB.
[37:58] Maya: That pattern works fine. We can reproduce the same embedding spec, and if you host privately you can keep embeddings on-prem. Watch out for tokenizer mismatch across vendors — we'll validate tokenization in the mapping run.

[40:10] Samir: What about model license / redistribution constraints? Together and Anthropic have different licenses. If we ship models in Private, are there restrictions?
[40:20] Carlos: License constraints depend on model origin. For models we curate, we document license. For Private, you still need to comply with the upstream license. We'll help surface those constraints in the mapping doc.

[42:45] Priya: Timeline-wise, if we wanted to pilot within 6 weeks, is that realistic?
[42:51] Maya: Yes — typical pilot: week 1 mapping + bench prep, week 2 bench runs, week 3 canary deploy on Dedicated or Hosted, week 4-6 iterate and run evals, quality checks. If Private is chosen, add 2-4 weeks for infra setup and KMS integration.

[45:00] Alex: Ok let's talk escalation: if we hit a blocking perf regression during canary, what's support look like?
[45:08] Devon: Enterprise customers get a named Technical Account Manager plus SE support. We can open fast-track kernel/quantization adjustments and push a hotfix in the runtime if needed.

[47:30] Samir: For our org, we need a single JSON lines of examples and then a small harness to replay traffic — do you provide any runner?
[47:38] Carlos: We have a small open-source replay harness and a Redshift/CSV ingestion pattern for traffic. We'll share links. It's a light wrapper — customers plug their anonymized logs and it replays to an endpoint under controlled qps.

[50:10] Priya: Security doc link?
[50:12] Maya: (posts link) https://redwood.example.com/compliance-pack/horizon — that'll be in the follow-up email too.

[51:35] Alex: Final recap please — what are the concrete next steps?
[51:40] Maya: Recap: 1) We'll send model-mapping matrix + cost sheet. 2) Carlos will run latency/cost benchmarks on your prompt seed set. 3) Schedule Private deployment scoping call (Priya, Samir, Carlos). 4) Share compliance bundle + KMS integration docs.
[51:58] Priya: Sounds good. Samir will coordinate the prompt set and traffic trace.
[52:05] Samir: Yep, I'll get that to you by Monday.
[52:10] Maya: Great. We'll aim to get bench results within a week of receiving the artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[52:17] Alex: Thanks all.
[52:20] (meeting ends)
